$comment: The source of sf-tabs's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/tabs (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

type.summary: The look (owner decision C96 item 1): no type or underline is the line (the default: a primary 2 px line under the selected label, on-surface ink), pills the plate (the selected tab on primary-container), vertical the menu's column (the current tab on the menu's current fill, labels at the start; on a phone the line with «Ещё»). full is retired: it draws the line with fit always (noted in SF.deprecations until 2027-01-01, journal value-tabs-full-to-underline).

scheme.summary: Retired (owner decision C96 item 1): the tabs draw one look per type whatever the scheme, so default, outline or link draw the same; outline and link are noted in SF.deprecations until 2027-01-01 (journal value-tabs-scheme-retired). The value is not a semantic color selector; custom templates may still read it.

items.x-markup: the attribute keeps the "label::flags|label" form or takes the list as JSON; key is read as an old name of id
items.summary: An item (set with setItems) may carry key (a stable id for the settings; the index otherwise), icon, count (a small counter after the label), href (an address; when every item has one the row is a strip of links -- a <nav> of <a> with the same look, the current one aria-current="page", no tablist, no arrows, Tab and Enter as links; one item with href among tabs is a tab that goes to its address) and pinned (never hidden, fixed in the settings); disabled (the tab stays focusable, says aria-disabled and selects nothing) and hint (a short text in the Framework tooltip on the tab, read as its description: for a disabled tab, why it is off); errors (the number of errors in the tab's panel: a count on the error container after the label, said with the name -- «Доступ, 2 ошибки»; setErrors({id: n}) gives them by id). The attribute takes the short form "label::flags|label" or a JSON array of the same items (R184 T13); a label holding | or :: is written in JSON.

overflow.summary: What the tabs do when they do not fit: more (the default: the tabs that do not fit go whole into a trailing «Ещё (n)» menu; the active one always stays in the row), scroll (the row scrolls), or wrap (rows wrap).

fit.summary: Whether the tabs share the row equally when they all fit, each at least its own width (owner decision C96 item 7): auto on a phone (below the md breakpoint) with two to four tabs, always, or never. What does not fit still goes into «Ещё (n)». Not for vertical tabs.

configurable.summary: A gear at the end of the tabs («Настроить вкладки») opens the standard menu with the tabs as a sortable list, a visibility checkbox per tab (pinned tabs fixed) and «Сбросить» in its footer. The choice is the host's: sf-tabs-settings-change {order, hidden}, sf-tabs-settings-reset, setSettings({order, hidden}).

lazy.summary: A panel is drawn when its tab is first opened, then kept drawn (its state stays when the person switches away). Until then the panel stands empty and hidden, so the tab's aria-controls still names it. sf-tabs-change for a first opening is sent once the panel is drawn. A page's own <div role="tabpanel"> panels are already in the page and are not affected.

hash.summary: The address keeps the selected tab: a tab the person chooses writes #<id> as a new history entry (path and query kept), so Back returns to the previous tab; on load, on Back and Forward and on a #link, #<id> of an item -- or of an element inside a panel -- opens that tab. Give each item an id. Off by default; one sf-tabs per page should use it. Not for a strip of links.

sticky.summary: The tab row stays in sight while its panels scroll past (position sticky at --sf-tabs-sticky-top, 0 by default), on the page surface. For long record and settings views.

selected.summary: the id of the selected tab's entry (its key, else its place)

settings-change.summary: The person ordered or showed/hid a tab in the settings; applied at once. The host keeps it and gives it back with setSettings.

settings-reset.summary: The person asked for the declared order back; the component shows it until the host answers with setSettings.

set-data.summary: Merges data into the current data (a function receives the current data and returns the next) and re-renders. tabs or items become tab items; panels or content become panels. A non-object is ignored.

set-panels.summary: Replaces the panels in the data (a function receives the current panels) and re-renders.

go-to.summary: Activates the tab at index (an index out of range means 0); does nothing for a disabled or the active tab. Sets active-index and emits sf-tabs-change.

go-to-error.summary: Opens the first tab, in the order the tabs stand, whose item has errors and focuses the first wrong field in its panel ([aria-invalid=true], [invalid] or :invalid), as a form's Save does after a failed check; refused with no-errors when none has. Not reported as a change.

relations.name: cl-menu-context
$comment: «Ещё» and the settings open the standard menu; the settings reorder with
sf-sortable and show and hide with sf-checkbox (owner, 2026-10-14).

relations.name: tooltip
$comment: A tab's hint is the Framework tooltip (component.tooltip), drawn only for an item with a hint.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-tabs for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split (the old detail from the element's adapter), host-attribute (no shim).

rows.note: the old detail adds component, tagName and template, which §8 takes out of the new one: the element's detail adapter makes it

x-summary: A tab list that shows one local panel at a time, with text or icon tabs given as attributes, slots or data, roving keyboard focus and linked tab panels.
x-renamed: settings.items: type string with a list default → list of {id, label, icon?, count?, href?, disabled?, pinned?} (§4.2, §16 item 42; key is read as id)
settings.size: the converter's number → enum 1/2, 1, 2 (the sheet's sizes; 1/2 is not a number)
events.sf-tab-change → change: the DOM name is sf-tabs-change (§8 <tag>-<verb>); the old name is a dated split alias whose detail keeps component, tagName and template
events.sf-tabs-settings-change, sf-tabs-settings-reset → settings-change, settings-reset: own verbs, the DOM names unchanged; component, tagName and template leave the detail (§8)
x-decisions:
version: 1.2.0 → 1.3.0, a minor (R184 tabs study, control/research/2026-11-12-tabs.md T3..T15): T3 an icon tab (variant="icons") draws the item's icon however it was given -- icon, or icon-start / icon-end of the "label::icon-start=home" form -- where it drew the button-icon default `add` on every tab; T14 a tab without a label is named in the page's language (runtime word tab, «Вкладка {n}» / «Tab {n}»), not the English «Tab N»; T12 sf-tabs-change is sent after the drawn tabs say aria-selected and the panels are shown or hidden (showSelection writes them at once; the next drawing writes the same), so a handler can focus a field of the new panel; T15 a panel slot whose host carried only its slot attribute (

, unwrapped by the base) gives its slot name to the tabpanel it fills, so [slot="panel-0"] still finds the panel after the drawing; a host the content keeps carries its own; data-sf-tab-panel="" stays the panel's own mark; T8 a panel is a tab stop of its own (tabindex=0) only when nothing in it takes the focus, checked after each drawing and when a part in a panel draws; a page panel written with a tabindex keeps it; the new setting lazy draws a panel when its tab is first opened and keeps it drawn, and sf-tabs-change for a first opening is sent once the panel is drawn; T9 a disabled tab is no longer the native disabled button: it stays focusable, says aria-disabled, the arrows reach it and a press or a key selects nothing; the tabs' sheet gives the class .disabled the buttons' disabled values; an item's hint (new item field) is the Framework tooltip on the tab (component.tooltip, lazy relation), read as its description -- for a disabled tab, why it is off; T4 when every item has an address (href) the row is a strip of links (owner decision C96 item 8): a

named as the tablist was, its items sf-button links () with the same look and the current one aria-current="page"; no tablist, no tab roles, no roving tab stop and no arrows (Tab and Enter, the browser's link keys, open in a new tab); a pressed link is followed by the browser and the strip marks it current; a panel beside the links is not a tabpanel, and the panel row is drawn only when a panel has content (root class sf-tabs--links); T10 the new setting hash keeps the selected tab in the address: a tab the person chooses writes # as a history entry (path and query kept), and on the first drawing, on Back, Forward and a #link the tab of # -- an item's id, or an element inside a panel -- opens (the first drawing without a change event); new setting sticky keeps the row in sight (position sticky at --sf-tabs-sticky-top, a seventh public variable, on the page surface). No closable tabs; C96 (owner decision 2026-11-12): two looks, the line (no type, underline) and the plate (pills); full and the outline/link schemes are retired aliases noted in SF.deprecations until 2027-01-01 (journal value-tabs-full-to-underline, value-tabs-scheme-retired, behaviour-tabs-line-default); the line is 2 px at every size and moves at once; only the selected label is medium, its width reserved; hover darkens the ink only; vertical draws the menu column and is a row with More below md; fit (auto|always|never) shares the row equally when two to four tabs fit, auto on the phone; per-tab errors read aloud, setErrors and go-to-error open the first tab with an error and focus its first invalid field.

version: 1.1.17 → 1.2.0, a minor: overflow defaults to more (owner decision C54, 2026-11-11; journal behaviour-tabs-overflow-more). Tabs that do not fit go whole into «Ещё (n)» in their order, the active and the pinned ones stay in the row; no fade, no scroll arrows. The former scrolling row is overflow="scroll". The row is laid out again when «Ещё (n)» changes its width with its count, when a tab draws late and when the text face arrives, so no tab stands clipped before the trigger. Also (C54 return D1, contract call 2026-11-11): when the pinned tabs and the current one do not fit beside «Ещё» together, a pinned tab gives way to the current one and goes into «Ещё», the last pinned first; the current tab left alone in the row and still wider than it is the only tab that may be shortened, with an ellipsis (class sf-tabs-squeezed); every other tab is whole in the row or in «Ещё». Also (C54 return D2): the row is laid out with the width «Ещё (n)» will have with its new count, measured in the trigger's text face before its button draws it, so a count of other digit widths no longer leaves the row 2 px past its room for a frame; of the rows that fit beside their own count the one with the most tabs is taken, so a row that comes back from a narrower box has the tabs it had at load.
version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, a minor while sf-tab-change holds a dated alias (§4.10).

events: the person's choice is `change`, sent as sf-tabs-change with {selected, previous, current, item, items} (§8 <tag>-<verb>; a DOM change would also be heard from a field inside a panel); the old sf-tab-change follows once through a split row whose adapter adds component, tagName and template. The migration's row to the bare `change` is corrected.
change reports a person (§8): a press, a key or «Ещё» send it; go-to, writing selected or active-index do not. The studio scenario asserts the attribute instead of the event.

own-verb-words: settings-change and settings-reset are verbs of the tabs alone (the person arranged or reset the tabs); their words are lang events.<verb>.label. Their DOM names stay sf-tabs-settings-change and sf-tabs-settings-reset, so no alias row is needed; the element left their detail (§8) -- no Framework code read it.
values: selected is the id of the selected entry (§7.2.3 binds values.selected); writing it, as a property or the attribute `selected`, selects that tab, and active-index stays the place.

manual activation (§7.2.1, §16 item 42): over a panel that holds a part with a deferred start ([data-sf-start]) the arrows, Home and End only move the focus and Enter or Space opens; otherwise the tabs keep automatic activation, as before. No setting: the panels decide.

opened (§7.2.1): a closed panel carries `hidden`, the open one does not. A page's or an assembly's own <div role="tabpanel"> children are the panels (§7.2.1 «A tab opens a part»): placed, never copied, shown by removing hidden and closed by setting it; a panel with data-entry="<id>" is the panel of that entry (§7.2.3), the others follow in order, and panels the assembly adds later are taken as they arrive.

actions: set-data {data, reason?}, set-panels {panels, reason?} and go-to {index} answer outcomes (§4.4) instead of the element; setItems, addItems, addPanels and setState stay helpers. settings is a writable object setting (the property); setSettings stays its helper (x-todo setter).
key-effects: the tablist's own keys; ArrowUp and ArrowDown act when type is vertical, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight otherwise (RTL turns them), «Ещё» is reached past the last tab.
a11y-name: aria-label or aria-labelledby on the host, carried to the tablist (the converter's "required"); the role is tablist, the host itself is a group.

instance ids (§7.1.1, simai/ui-source#41): tab, panel and label ids came from a module counter (sf-smart-tabs-<n>); they are the host's path id and a local name now, <path>--tab-<n>, --panel-<n>, --label-<n>. The class tabs (component/tabs, component/tab) likewise: <path>--<part>-<n>.
item-shape: items name their fields with `of` (id, label, icon, count, href, disabled, pinned); a constant list in an assembly gives only the id, its label is lang roles.<role>.items.<id> (§11.3).
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus «Ещё», configurable tabs and entries with ids; probe.json drives the arrows, Home, End, Enter, Space and Tab, automatic and manual (gate 16).
css-variables: the six public variables the sheet already reads (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).
side-effects: none; «Ещё» and the settings open sf-context-menu, whose own layer they are.
docs: docs/docs.md, where the folder keeps it (as sf-tooltip).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.2: the page-panel watch (a MutationObserver on the host) runs while the element is in the page: it stops when the element is taken out and starts again, with the panels added meanwhile, when it is placed again (§7.7, gate 36).
version 1.1.3: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.1.5: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.8: in type="pills" the selected tab is the only filled one; the other tabs are text on the surface with no fill and no border whatever the scheme, painted only by the surface state layer (4 hover, 8 keyboard focus, 12 pressed), light and dark, any theme colour (owner, effects.simai.io, 2026-11-01). A repair, no new name: scheme="outline" is no longer needed for this look. Class sheet src/component/tabs 1.0.1.

version 1.1.10: the standard menu (sf-context-menu) and the settings list's elements are asked for through SF.Loader.ensure (core.runtime 1.19.0), not a race of whenDefined against 3 s of its own (reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 4). No change to what the tabs draw or say.

version 1.1.12 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.13: the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws are asked for their current names (appearance ghost for link, status danger for error; actions block, decisions C13 and C15), so the template uses no dated alias; nothing it draws changes.

version 1.1.16: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives the action's method its one object argument, goTo({index}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object); the element's code also takes the value alone, goTo(<number>), and the reference says so (x-registry.action-calls). setData(data, reason?) and setPanels(panels, reason?) stay positional in the reference, as the element's methods take them: given one object, they read it as the data or the panels themselves (x-registry.action-calls positional). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: the «Ещё» and settings menus it places on the body take the density of the tabs (or the normal ladder under an explicit size), and the sizes it gives them are relative (density, decision C22). Also: a patch, nothing drawn differently. setData and setPanels take the object form of their action too (standard §4.4): setData({data, reason}) merges data, where it merged the wrapper object and answered applied, and setPanels({panels, reason}) replaces the panels, where it cleared them. The runtime gives the class-written methods that form (elementFromManifest's positional, core.runtime 1.43.0); setData(data, reason) and setPanels(panels, reason) stay as they were. The reference gives both one object argument (x-registry.action-calls no longer says positional). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.17 (2026-11-11, audit of dead Smart sheets): sf-tabs has no Smart sheet any more. Its bundle imported js/templates/default.css while its rule has no css, so the Loader never asked for smart/tabs/css/tabs.css and no page ever had those rules. Force-linking the sheet on every snapshot and three extra cases changed only type="full": the setData-component tab's width (TB-04, fixed in the class sheet on fix/content-precheck) and the seam between tabs. The seam rule moved to the tabs class sheet (tabs 1.1.1): the full row draws one 1px seam between its buttons where it drew two (2px of primary-active), as the class markup always did (tests/tabs-layout-scope: no double seam). The other rules (display: contents of the hosts, min-width 0, flex) changed nothing on any page and are gone with the file. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-tabs when the interface needs the tabs behavior.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: Built-in text/icon tabs use one enabled native tab stop and linked panels. Navigation arrows follow orientation and RTL, reach disabled tabs (aria-disabled, focusable, selecting nothing), wrap, focus and activate. A panel is a tab stop only when nothing in it takes the focus. Perpendicular arrows and nested widget keys remain local. A custom tab component descriptor is presentation-only: its named wrapper remains the single tab stop and the rendered Smart visual is inert.

item.description: A normalised tab item: label plus what was given (disabled, icon, component and so on).

items.description: A normalised tab item: label plus what was given (disabled, icon, component and so on).

getData.summary: Returns the data set with setData: {tabs, panels, ...}; {tabs: [], panels: []} when none was set.

setItems.summary: Replaces the tabs in the data (a function receives the current tabs) and re-renders.

setState.summary: Writes each key as its kebab-case attribute; an array (items) is serialised as label::flags entries joined by |. false, null, undefined or empty removes the attribute, true sets it empty.

onTabChange.summary: Adds a listener for sf-tabs-change; the handler is called with (current, detail, event). Ignores a non-function handler.

setSettings.summary: Applies the person's stored arrangement: {order: [keys], hidden: [keys]}. A key the items no longer have is ignored; an item the order does not name follows in its declared place, visible; a pinned tab is never hidden; the active tab is shown in place even when hidden.

setErrors.summary: Gives the errors of each panel by entry id ({profile: 0, access: 2}); the tabs show the count and say it with the tab's name. An id not given keeps the item's own errors.
